## DETAILS

### Scope and current behavior

- All document families support editing through `GuiDocumentCommonInterface`, but their current `EditMode` still determines what user input may do. `GuiDocumentViewer` and its `GuiMultilineTextBox` subclass inherit scrolling. `GuiDocumentLabel`, XML `DocumentTextBox`, and `GuiSinglelineTextBox` use the label implementation. Calling the latter family non-scrollable means it has no `GuiScrollView` gesture scrolling; preserve its existing internal offset used to keep the caret visible.
- Keep recognition and selection in Core. No new renderer behavior, remote-protocol messages, selection handles or rendering primitives are required. Rebuild the Core used by GacJS; an HTTP browser test against native Core does not verify a stale Wasm binary.

### Press offers and deferred clicks

- The actual Started fields are `generateLeftButtonClick` and `generateRightButtonClick`. They default to true and must control only deferred mouse generation, not whether an eligible press gesture is offered. Retain the existing successful-single-contact criteria: one Down, no excursion beyond the eight-logical-unit radius, and successful End. Final-Up displacement participates; crossing the radius and returning, an extra contact, or cancellation permanently disqualifies the press.
- Resolve the overlap in the current click recognizers explicitly: the left-click recognizer currently has no duration ceiling. Offer exactly one press kind at End, short below 500000 microseconds and long at or above 500000 microseconds. Do not offer a short press after a declined long press: the document's short-press selection-preservation handler could otherwise swallow the right click requested by a long press on selected text. Long pressing is still recognized on successful release, not by a timer while held.
- If the offered press is not selected, preserve the existing fallback matrix:

  | Enabled click flags | Short press | Long press |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Both | Left click | Right click |
  | Left only | Left click | Left click |
  | Right only | None | Right click |
  | Neither | None | None |

  The gesture offer occurs independently of this table. Selecting any gesture suppresses both fallback clicks, including a selected press whose recognizer would otherwise have cached a click. `handled` alone does not select a gesture or veto fallback. Preserve sticky selection and the existing scrolling/manipulation priority once either has been selected.
- Add typed short-press and long-press payload alternatives to `GuiPointGestureEventArgs::gesture` in `<GacUI repo>/Source/Application/GraphicsCompositions/GuiGraphicsEventReceiver.h`. Keep the existing scrolling/manipulation alternatives in their current order and append the press alternatives consistently. Each press needs a position: use the original first-contact screen point reprojected into the accepted composition's current logical coordinates at End, matching deferred-click targeting. Successful End already has empty contact slots, so consumers cannot obtain this from `Points[0]`.
- Register the payload types and fields in `<GacUI repo>/Source/Reflection/TypeDescriptors/GuiReflectionEvents.cpp` and the type list in `<GacUI repo>/Source/Reflection/TypeDescriptors/GuiReflectionPlugin.h`. Update exact Workflow variant constructors and reflection assertions to the expanded ordered type. Preserve copy-on-extraction and whole-variant assignment semantics; do not introduce an object-valued replacement API.
- Preserve raw Action before recognition, recognizer End before public End, and capture cleanup before synthetic MouseMove/Down/Up. Both event source fields identify the accepted composition. Deliver one public End even when a press is selected; retain independent physical mouse capture/button state. Keep the current UI-thread and deferred-composition-removal lifetime rules.

### Shared document integration

- Replace the current `GuiDocumentCommonInterface::OnPointSequenceStarted` rejection gate, which marks Selectable/Editable content handled without accepting. Merely enabling `AcceptPointEvents` cannot overcome that gate. Enable default point acceptance for the label family as well as the already-enabled scroll-view family, and retain both click flags as true for ordinary document operation.
- Add the proposed `pointEventComposition` installation argument and put shared press handling in `GuiDocumentCommonInterface`. Use each control's persistent bounds composition, also the scroll-view gesture target, rather than the template-dependent mouse area or `GetPointEventComposition()` (an active-capture query that is null while idle). Retain the existing mouse-area cursor and mouse-handler replacement behavior. Do not duplicate point subscriptions after template refresh or overwrite an earlier accepted child composition or an application's explicit click suppression.
- Apply document press handling only to document-content starts. Scrollbars, surrounding chrome and embedded controls must retain their own input behavior. Gestures do not bubble: a child that accepts its own sequence remains the sole owner. Scrollable document content must accept at the same bounds target used by `GuiScrollView`, allowing its existing scrolling consumer and optional `MomentumScrolling` component to work.
- Convert the press position from the point event composition into current document coordinates before `CalculateCaretFromPoint`, accounting for margins, the viewer's scrolled composition and the label's internal view offset. `GetMouseOffset()` is relative to the mouse area and cannot be reused unchanged for a bounds-relative gesture. Use the existing nearest-caret calculation instead of implementing another text hit tester.
- For selection membership, normalize `CaretBegin`/`CaretEnd` for comparison without changing their direction. For a nonempty range, a nearest-caret hit at either boundary counts as on the selection; caret positions are boundaries between characters. A collapsed range is the current caret, not a selection. Check current document state when the press is delivered.
- In enabled Selectable/Editable content:
  - Short press on a nonempty selection selects and handles the short gesture, focuses the control and preserves both endpoints. Otherwise decline it and let the normal deferred left click position the caret, preserving ordinary mouse modifier semantics.
  - Long press with a collapsed selection and a different hit caret focuses the control, extends from the current caret to the hit caret, and selects/handles the gesture. Reuse the existing movement path so caret visibility, selection notification and viewport adjustment stay consistent.
  - Long press on the current caret or anywhere in an existing nonempty selection declines the gesture and generates the normal right click without changing endpoints. For the unspecified case of long pressing outside an existing selection, also retain that range and use normal right-click fallback: range creation is requested only when no selection exists, and the current right-mouse handler does not move the caret. Do not add a context-menu implementation merely to demonstrate right-click delivery.
- ViewOnly must not move the caret or select text through the new press handlers; preserve hyperlink activation through ordinary click fallback and scrolling where available. Selectable permits range changes but no editing; Editable retains normal editing. Disabled controls must not focus or change selection. Physical mouse dragging, Shift-click and keyboard selection continue to use their existing paths.
- A drag over accepted scrollable document content now scrolls while retaining selection, instead of streaming mouse input to extend the range. The label family gains press selection but no scrolling gesture consumer. Neither family should select manipulation automatically. Presses alone must not start momentum; a fresh Started must still stop existing momentum before the new selection action.

## No.1 Offer exclusive End-time presses and consume document selection on the persistent point target

Keep the existing recognizer order and lifecycle. Both click recognizers track single-contact eligibility independently of click-generation flags. At successful End, the right-click recognizer offers a long press at or above 500000 microseconds; the left-click recognizer offers a short press below that boundary. Deferred fallback remains separately controlled by the completed Started flags, including left-only fallback after a declined long press. Any selected gesture suppresses every fallback click. Existing radial movement, extra-contact and cancellation checks remain authoritative.

Append typed short/long press payloads to the gesture variant. Reproject the saved original screen start into the accepted composition's current logical coordinates at End, while capture is still valid. Register both payloads and expand exact reflected/Workflow variant tests without changing existing alternative indices or value-copy semantics.

Install shared document Started/gesture subscriptions once on each control's persistent bounds composition, which is also the scroll viewer's point target. Track whether the original hit belongs to document content and exclude chrome and embedded controls. Remove the old mouse-area rejection gate and enable point events by default for the label family. Do not rewrite acceptance or click flags. Translate the press position through current composition bounds before document hit testing, so scrolling, label offsets and template replacement remain correct.

For enabled Selectable/Editable documents, consume a short press inside an existing inclusive range without moving endpoints; consume a long press at a different caret only when the range is collapsed, extending through the existing Move path. Focus only consumed selections. Decline all other presses for ordinary click fallback. Preserve ViewOnly hyperlinks, disabled behavior, physical mouse/keyboard selection and existing scrolling/momentum arbitration.

Extend ordinary deterministic lifecycle, coordinate, reflection and exact document selection tests; update useful scrolling/selection snapshots and existing live fixtures. Validate metadata, all consumer modes, the full unit suite and available native/remote/browser paths. Keep authored, generated and snapshot commits separate.

### CODE CHANGE

Appended `GuiPointGesture_ShortPressing` and `GuiPointGesture_LongPressing` with reflected `position` fields. Click recognizers now keep eligibility independent of fallback flags, offer only their exclusive duration at End, and the manager returns no fallback after any gesture selection. Shared document installation owns persistent bounds-level Started/gesture subscriptions; the old template mouse-area rejection subscription is removed. Content-origin filtering, current composition coordinate conversion and the existing Move operation implement selection without rewriting click flags or acceptance. Labels enable point acceptance by default.

The initial verification changes extend the ordinary click matrix with typed payloads, radial/final-Up/extra-contact/cancellation/reset and moving-gesture arbitration assertions; expand reflection and Workflow compile checks; and add exact ordinary document range/focus/click assertions using the existing renderer and point-input helpers without emitting snapshots. Existing document snapshots now demonstrate short/long press selection and accepted scrolling across template refresh, and document momentum runs in all three edit modes.
